dominant_breach: private compute demand can be treated as strategic infrastructure while grid, water, utility, and municipal costs are carried by public systems or ordinary ratepayers without public-upside recovery
fastest_washout: ratebase cost shifting, water-permit conflict, interconnection backlog, reliability reserve cost, and tax-abatement leakage wash out local public gains

public_balance_sheet_gate.note: AI data-center load growth is now a live public-balance-sheet case with concrete state/utility tariff instruments, not only national load forecasts: transmission, generation, ratebase, water, tax-abatement, reliability, minimum-bill, collateral, exit-fee, and reporting obligations must be assigned before compute capacity can be certified as public wealth. Rev0349 separates instrument-bound evidence from remaining project-packet proof debt: PPL LP-6 and PUC approval are live regulatory instruments, JLARC is state-audit incidence evidence, and ICPRB is basin-water modeling; signed ESAs, compliance tariffs, facility water packets, class-cost studies, and abatement contracts still decide pass/fail. Rev0350 adds the Louisiana/Meta Richland Parish packet as a named project-level stress test: LPSC U-37425 is an open generation/transmission docket for service to a single customer; Entergy says the approved/revised arrangements make Meta pay its share/full cost of service and produce $2.65 billion in customer benefits; adversarial docket filings challenge whether ESA term, net-energy-cost, abandonment, sponsor/lease, and financing risks could still leave ordinary ratepayers exposed. This turns signed-ESA proof debt into a concrete docket packet rather than a generic future task. Rev0351 closes the narrow U-37425 written-order proof debt but does not comfort-clear the project: Order No. U-37425 accepts the settlement and certifies generation/transmission resources subject to conditions, yet Staff did not approve the ESA and Related Agreements. The open risk is now condition performance: CIAC accounting, parent guaranty/collateral, early-termination fee treatment, annual confidential usage/demand/billing reports, material modification notices, and customer-caused transmission or power-quality upgrade cost exclusion. Rev0351 also adds U-37882 Project Evest and X-37921 statewide large-load guidelines as live expansion/reopen triggers. Exact rev0351 audit phrase: ESA and Related Agreements not approved. Rev0352 converts the Louisiana large-load router into a public-balance-sheet test matrix: the LPSC guidelines require proof of load shape, resource adequacy, cost assignment, stranded-asset protection, curtailment, fuel, market/FAC, environmental/local impacts, and ongoing oversight. Project Evest testimony now supplies inspectable project claims but not complete comfort: May testimony identifies seven CCCTs, three battery resources, over 250 miles of new 500kV/230kV transmission, roughly $13B generation capital, quarterly monitoring, and ongoing prudence review, while key transmission totals, HSPM/AEO exhibits, and ESA/MMC details remain redacted or sealed. Rev0353 separates three ledgers that had been too compressed: resource adequacy stress (S521-S522), private contract/financing protections (S523/S525), and local public-service claims (S524/S526). This lowers proof debt conceptually but keeps the public-balance-sheet gate blocked until utility-service/tariff, water, incentive, and stranded-cost instruments are public or auditably summarized. Rev0354 adds River Bend/Hut 8 indenture and project-scale proof plus Louisiana sales/use tax exemption, Act 434 ad valorem/PILOT authority, local water/electric-infrastructure claims, and a $26B adversarial public-cost model; private creditor seniority remains separate from public hold-harmless proof. Rev0355 adds River Bend public-instrument discipline: Entergy utility-capacity/timeline evidence (330 MW utility capacity for 245 MW critical IT load), local IDB/PILOT leaseback and up-to-$90M/year revenue claims, an IDB distribution-schedule claim, rebate-sequencing evidence, and an official parish public-records route. These sources make the public-upside claim auditable but keep certification blocked until the actual PILOT lease, distribution resolution, utility-service/tariff terms, switchyard/line-cost assignment, water transfer agreement, exemption/Quality Jobs awards, and load-vs-forecast/ratebase evidence are bound.

ai_data_center_grid_water_backstop.note: DOE/LBNL electricity-use forecasts, FERC large-load/co-location proceedings, PJM/EIA localized load evidence, and state/utility tariff decisions now make compute infrastructure a current cost-allocation and reliability-backstop problem. Rev0348 adds Ohio, Virginia, Pennsylvania, and Wisconsin tariff/service-agreement instruments, showing the pass/fail hinge is whether take-or-pay, collateral, exit-fee, no-stranded-cost, and public-transparency terms actually protect existing customers. Rev0349 adds concrete project/jurisdiction incidence evidence: PPL LP-6 settlement/approval, Virginia state-audit cost/tax/water exposure, and Potomac basin water modeling. The case now distinguishes enforceable or decision-bound instruments from remaining project-packet proof debt instead of expanding doctrine. Rev0350 adds Louisiana U-37425 as the first named mega-campus counterparty packet: three CCGTs, new transmission, 1,500 MW solar authority, a revised $2B additional-savings claim, and adversarial testimony/motion evidence on 15-year ESA, cost-allocation, and financing/lease risk. The case now requires paired utility/regulator/intervenor treatment for every megaproject rather than accepting either project benefits or opposition claims alone. Rev0351 moves Louisiana from a single Meta/Laidley docket to a project family and policy router: U-37425 has a written conditioned order, U-37882 is an open adjacent Project Evest docket, and X-37921 creates a statewide large-load-guidelines repository. Project Evest is especially risky because the public application claims about $2.67 billion in benefits over a 20-year ESA but seeks approval for a much larger generation/transmission stack under redacted HSPM/AEO terms. Rev0352 adds the official LPSC large-load guidelines and Project Evest testimony. This is real movement because the case can now be scored against named categories instead of generalized concerns: load characteristics, resource adequacy/capacity, transmission/interconnection, stranded asset and exit risk, rate design/cost recovery, operational control/curtailment, ancillary services/power quality, fuel supply, ramp management, market/planning impacts, environmental/local impacts, and ongoing oversight. The same evidence keeps the case failed because Beauchamp’s guideline-compliance mapping depends on HSPM/AEO material and sealed exhibits for the highest-risk terms. Rev0353 adds Louisiana resource-adequacy and River Bend project evidence. Order X-37566 supplies measurable statewide reserve-margin stress rather than generic capacity anxiety, including outer-year negative summer reserve-margin scenarios and explicit large-data-center/AI load context. The May 2026 technical conference clarifies that the Lightning process accelerates MBM review but does not bypass Commission certification. River Bend adds a separate project packet: 330 MW initial Entergy utility capacity, 245 MW critical IT load, 15-year private lease, Google-backed payment obligations, $3.25B senior secured non-recourse notes, and a $16M water-infrastructure commitment. The case still fails because these private financing and company water claims do not prove household/ratepayer hold-harmless terms without utility-service, tariff, water-permit, and local-agreement records. Rev0354 adds River Bend/Hut 8 indenture and project-scale proof plus Louisiana sales/use tax exemption, Act 434 ad valorem/PILOT authority, local water/electric-infrastructure claims, and a $26B adversarial public-cost model; private creditor seniority remains separate from public hold-harmless proof. Rev0354 exact River Bend site phrase for validation: 2,361 acres under option with a 627-acre site footprint; private creditor seniority remains distinct from public proof.

large_load_utility_cost_shift.note: Large-load service must prove collateral, direct-assignment, minimum-bill, demand-ratchet, exit-fee, termination-charge, and no-stranded-cost protection. Rev0348 partially closes the prior generic tariff proof debt: AEP Ohio Schedule DCT supplies load-study fees, ramp, collateral, minimum-demand, reassignment, BTM generation, and exit-fee mechanics; Virginia SCC supplies GS-5, 14-year, 85% T&D, 60% generation, and collateral safeguards; Pennsylvania supplies a model-tariff proceeding with CIAC, tiered collateral, and minimum contract terms; Wisconsin supplies We Energies/Alliant tariff and service-agreement decisions with 15-year term, lower threshold, transmission-cost, termination-charge, reporting, and transparency modifications. Exact tariff tokens preserved for audit: collateral can equal 50% of total minimum charges; minimum demand charges can be capped at 85% of contract capacity; Virginia uses a 14-year contract obligation. Rev0349 adds project-level rate-case substance: PPL LP-6 covers 50 MW single-facility and 75 MW aggregate-within-10-mile-radius large loads, requires at least a 10-year ESA, enhanced credit/security, mandatory exit fees, upgrade security/CIAC, non-critical load segmentation, and $11 million annual USR assignment to LP-6 after approval. These details turn generic tariff safeguards into a concrete PPL/Pennsylvania test packet rather than a model-tariff placeholder. Rev0350 adds the Louisiana/Meta U-37425 cost-shift packet: official docket status, Entergy approval/current agreement surfaces, Kunkel testimony, and the financing-risk motion. The evidence preserves both sides: Entergy asserts Meta pays its share/full cost of service and $2.65B total customer benefits; the intervenor record argues a 15-year ESA with extensions, redacted CIAC/ESA terms, possible higher net energy costs, and Blue Owl/Beignet sponsor restructuring can leave ratepayers exposed unless final ESA terms, FAC credits, collateral, abandonment, and no-stranded-cost protections are verified. Rev0351 audit/refactor: do not keep asking generically for a written LPSC order once it exists. The live burden is whether order conditions actually prevent cost shift: FRP recovery and prudence reviews, zero plant-in-service treatment for contributed costs, true-up of minimum monthly charges, parent guaranties/collateral/credit insurance, early-termination fee filings, 30-day modification/cancellation notices, and exclusion of solely customer-caused transmission/power-quality upgrades from other-customer rates. U-37882 adds a second adjacent load queue before U-37425 conditions can be empirically observed. Exact rev0351 audit phrase: ESA and Related Agreements not approved. Rev0352 adds a sharper Louisiana cost-shift audit. The guidelines require network/interconnection costs caused by the load to be fully assigned, no material transmission costs shifted without commensurate benefits, rates that recover the full incremental revenue requirement, no cross-subsidization, and protection against early termination. May and Beauchamp testimony claim MMC/FRP/FAC/CIAC and customer revenue protections, but several decisive tokens are still redacted or sealed, so the pass/fail hinge is now a redaction table rather than another doctrine paragraph. Rev0353 sharpens the ratepayer-incidence test: S521 shows capacity/reserve-margin pressure in the same state where U-37425, U-37882, and River Bend loads are emerging, and S522 shows Commissioners and stakeholders asking whether large loads bring their own capacity, fuel, and monitoring obligations. Hut 8/Google backstop evidence protects a private lease payment stream; it is not itself proof that utility network, fuel, FAC/FRP, stranded-asset, or post-term costs are not shifted to ordinary customers. Rev0354 adds River Bend/Hut 8 indenture and project-scale proof plus Louisiana sales/use tax exemption, Act 434 ad valorem/PILOT authority, local water/electric-infrastructure claims, and a $26B adversarial public-cost model; private creditor seniority remains separate from public hold-harmless proof.

data_center_water_consumption_permitting.note: Water and wastewater capacity must be scored by basin stress, cooling technology, drought scenario, local/tribal claim, and enforceable mitigation rather than treated as ordinary siting detail. Rev0349 closes the basin-level water proof gap for Northern Virginia/Potomac but not the facility packet: JLARC says current data-center water demand is sustainable but oversight must account for growth; ICPRB estimates WMA data-center water use at about 4 MGD average and 15 MGD peak-day in 2025, with baseline 2050 projections of about 22 MGD average and over 80 MGD peak. The remaining proof debt is facility-level water contracts, daily/monthly reporting, cooling mode, drought curtailment, wastewater/discharge treatment, and local/tribal claim incidence. Rev0352 adds Louisiana environmental/local-impact guideline coverage, but not facility water proof. The guidelines require identification of environmental and local impacts and assignment of mitigation/compliance costs; Project Evest still lacks public facility-level withdrawal, cooling, discharge, wastewater, drought, and local-service-burden evidence. Rev0353 adds River Bend water proof but keeps the water gate blocked: Hut 8 says it will fund a $16M well, roughly eight miles of water main, and system upgrades transferred to West Feliciana Parish at no taxpayer cost, with closed-loop cooling and no local-supply-impact claims. Missing evidence remains the actual water/wastewater agreements, withdrawal and discharge permits, drought and curtailment rules, operating data, and who pays if parish infrastructure costs exceed the company commitment. River Bend now has project-specific support for water, PILOT/rebate, electric-infrastructure, and incentive claims, but still needs primary agreements, ratebase/FAC/FRP treatment, permits, and clawback documentation.

compute_infrastructure_public_subsidy_re.note: Public loans, tax abatements, grid upgrades, water-system investments, and special contracts require clawbacks, public-upside sharing, minimum service commitments, reporting, transparent service agreements, and no-stranded-cost clauses. Rev0348 adds live tariff/service-agreement examples where regulators are explicitly converting vague economic-development upside into minimum-term, collateral, termination-charge, full-cost, and transparency safeguards. Rev0349 adds the fiscal-subsidy flank: Virginia JLARC reports the state data-center sales/use tax exemption produced $928 million in FY23 tax savings and is used by about 90 percent of the industry, so abatement/exemption recapture and public-upside terms must be scored alongside tariff collateral and no-stranded-cost rules. Rev0350 adds sponsor/financing recapture risk: the motion for investigation flags Blue Owl/Beignet restructuring and lease/ownership changes as a distinct public-balance-sheet problem, so full-cost service claims must be cross-checked against parent guarantees, collateral, abandonment terms, and enforceable public-upside recovery. Rev0351 adds recapture specificity: U-37425 customer-protection terms must be monitored through CIAC, guarantee/collateral, early-termination, and reporting instruments, while U-37882/Project Evest benefit claims and low-income/weatherization contributions remain application claims until embedded in signed agreements and Commission orders. Rev0352 adds a recapture/process refactor: Power to Care, weatherization, sustainability, and claimed customer-benefit commitments are not scored as public-upside recovery unless they are tied to enforceable ESA/order/reporting terms. The X-37921 notice also shows that the statewide guideline process is a repository/comment process with no interventions accepted, so it supplies policy surveillance but not adversarial proof. Comments are due June 19, 2026. Rev0353 adds the public incentive side of River Bend: LED says the project is expected to use the state data-center tax rebate and Quality Jobs program. Those are not automatically illegitimate, but they create recapture proof debt: clawbacks, job/accountability terms, local PILOT/TIF/abatement interactions, public-upside sharing, and whether private Google-backed cash flows generate any public seniority return beyond general development claims. Rev0354 adds River Bend/Hut 8 indenture and project-scale proof plus Louisiana sales/use tax exemption, Act 434 ad valorem/PILOT authority, local water/electric-infrastructure claims, and a $26B adversarial public-cost model; private creditor seniority remains separate from public hold-harmless proof. Rev0355 adds River Bend public-instrument discipline: Entergy utility-capacity/timeline evidence (330 MW utility capacity for 245 MW critical IT load), local IDB/PILOT leaseback and up-to-$90M/year revenue claims, an IDB distribution-schedule claim, rebate-sequencing evidence, and an official parish public-records route. These sources make the public-upside claim auditable but keep certification blocked until the actual PILOT lease, distribution resolution, utility-service/tariff terms, switchyard/line-cost assignment, water transfer agreement, exemption/Quality Jobs awards, and load-vs-forecast/ratebase evidence are bound.

place_public_finance_gate.note: Local grids, substations, transmission, water, and tax-base deals can turn compute siting into place-based service-wealth reallocation. The EIA Virginia/Dominion evidence turns this from a national electricity-demand forecast into a local public-finance and ratepayer-incidence problem; rev0348 adds tariff/service-agreement instruments showing how regulators are trying to keep existing customers from becoming residual payers. Rev0349 makes the place-finance burden more concrete: Pennsylvania LP-6 shows an approved customer-class and ESA structure; Virginia JLARC shows state and local fiscal/water exposure; ICPRB shows basin-scale water demand and reliability planning exposure. Rev0350 adds Louisiana/Richland Parish as a named place-finance test: a single-customer project can drive generation, transmission, solar procurement, local development claims, and ratepayer-risk disputes across a regional utility system. Rev0351 adds a Louisiana large-load router: Project Evest sits adjacent to the U-37425 Laidley/Meta site in Richland Parish, and the X-37921 repository docket means parish/site-specific generation, transmission, tax, water, and ratepayer effects should be tracked alongside statewide large-load guideline evolution. Rev0352 makes the local incidence more concrete: Project Evest testimony places the adjacent Richland Parish load inside a generation/transmission buildout with seven proposed CCCTs, three battery resources, new substations, and long 500kV/230kV lines, while the guidelines require environmental/local impacts and mitigation-cost assignment. Facility water, wastewater, local tax, and parish-level service-load packets remain missing. Rev0353 localizes the project incidence in West Feliciana Parish: official LED materials identify up to $10B phase-one investment, 330 MW initial utility capacity, 245 MW critical IT load, and expected incentive use; Hut 8 separately claims a $16M water-infrastructure buildout transferred to the parish at no taxpayer cost. The cube now needs the actual local agreements, water operating duties, incentive awards, clawbacks, and public-service burden allocation. River Bend now has project-specific support for water, PILOT/rebate, electric-infrastructure, and incentive claims, but still needs primary agreements, ratebase/FAC/FRP treatment, permits, and clawback documentation.

utility_affordability_burden.note: Existing households and small businesses become residual payers if large-load growth is over-forecast or infrastructure costs are socialized through rates. Rev0348 upgrades this from proxy to direct tariff evidence: Ohio, Virginia, Pennsylvania, and Wisconsin instruments all frame minimum terms, collateral, cost-causation, transmission-cost, reporting, and exit/termination provisions as protections for existing customers. Exact tariff tokens preserved for audit: 50% of total minimum charges, 85% of contract capacity, and 14-year contract. Rev0349 keeps affordability in scope: the final PUC approval reports a 4.9% projected residential-bill increase for a 918 kWh customer, while the large-load provisions add long-term commitments, minimum demand guarantees, financial protections, and cost-causation alignment; Virginia JLARC estimates Dominion residential generation/transmission costs could rise $14 to $37 per month by 2040 under data-center-driven demand scenarios. Rev0350 adds a direct affordability-risk contrast: Entergy claims $2B additional and $2.65B total customer benefits from the Meta agreements, while Kunkel testimony says the application could put other ratepayers at risk of hundreds of millions, if not billions, and identifies net energy cost and transmission/operating cost allocation channels. The case therefore scores Louisiana as contested, not comfort-cleared. Rev0351 tightens affordability evidence from claimed benefits to monitorable conditions. For U-37425, the order has customer-protection conditions but also preserves non-approval of the ESA and Related Agreements; for U-37882, the application claims $2.67B in benefits over a 20-year ESA term, yet the hearing schedule makes this a live 2026 record rather than settled evidence. Rev0352 narrows the affordability question: the record now has customer-savings and bill-protection claims tied to MMCs, FRP, FAC, CIAC, monitoring, and guideline compliance, but the same record identifies redactions and future prudence review. Existing customers are therefore not comfort-cleared until actual load-versus-forecast, revenue-requirement, cost-recovery, FAC, and reporting data are visible. Rev0353 adds a statewide affordability stress context through X-37566 reserve-margin forecasts and the large-load technical conference. The River Bend private lease/backstop may reduce sponsor default risk but does not equal customer affordability protection unless utility rates, fuel riders, network upgrades, and future shortfall costs are explicitly insulated from households and small businesses. River Bend now has project-specific support for water, PILOT/rebate, electric-infrastructure, and incentive claims, but still needs primary agreements, ratebase/FAC/FRP treatment, permits, and clawback documentation.

water_wastewater_need_pressure.note: Water and wastewater systems need a claimant-perimeter test before compute facilities are treated as ordinary economic development. Rev0349 adds ICPRB basin modeling and JLARC state-audit water warnings; the case now has basin-level water stress evidence, while facility-level withdrawal, cooling, discharge, and drought-curtailment documents remain missing. Rev0352 does not close water proof debt. It only adds a Louisiana guideline hook for environmental/local impacts; facility water and wastewater packets are still required before this case can certify local service-wealth protection. Rev0353 moves water from abstract concern to a named local service packet. The River Bend water commitment is concrete enough to track as evidence, but still company-claim caveated until parish transfer agreements, permit files, maintenance obligations, peak demand, wastewater impacts, and drought-contingency rules are in the cube. River Bend now has project-specific support for water, PILOT/rebate, electric-infrastructure, and incentive claims, but still needs primary agreements, ratebase/FAC/FRP treatment, permits, and clawback documentation.

public_backstop_seniority_waterfall.note: The default waterfall protects uptime and speed-to-power first unless tariff/service-agreement instruments make existing ratepayers, water users, and municipalities senior. Rev0348 adds direct evidence of emerging safeguards: minimum-term/take-or-pay obligations, collateral, demand ratchets, exit or termination charges, full-cost resource models, transparency, and reporting mechanisms. Exact tariff tokens preserved for audit: 50% of total minimum charges, 85% of contract capacity, and 14-year contract. Rev0349 seniority refactor: existing ratepayers and water users cannot be treated as residual claimants when approved LP-6 terms, state-audit risk estimates, and basin-water projections show identifiable cost and resource-incidence channels. Rev0350 refines seniority: when a utility asserts full-cost-service customer benefits but intervenor filings identify ESA/CIAC, fuel/energy, abandonment, and financing risks, the cube must keep ordinary ratepayers senior until the final signed ESA, parent/sponsor guarantees, collateral schedule, and no-stranded-cost clauses are inspectable. Rev0351 seniority refactor: ordinary customers are not subordinated merely because an order contains protective conditions. Seniority is proven only when the condition chain is inspectable and enforceable: CIAC zeroing, collateral/parent guarantee seniority, early-termination proceeds, material modification notice, annual usage/demand/billing reports, and no other-customer recovery for customer-caused transmission/power-quality upgrades. Rev0352 seniority refactor: the LPSC guidelines name seniority-relevant terms directly—cost assignment, stranded-asset protection, early-termination protection, curtailment, fuel-risk assignment, environmental mitigation, and ongoing oversight. Project Evest must therefore be tracked through a guideline-by-guideline public-redaction matrix; sealed HSPM/AEO exhibits cannot by themselves establish that ordinary ratepayers are senior. Rev0353 seniority refactor: private creditors and landlords now have visible seniority evidence—Google-backed pass-through obligations and first-priority secured notes, non-recourse to Hut 8 Corp.—while public seniority remains less visible. The cube should not let private backstop specificity masquerade as ratepayer/public hold-harmless proof. Rev0354 adds River Bend/Hut 8 indenture and project-scale proof plus Louisiana sales/use tax exemption, Act 434 ad valorem/PILOT authority, local water/electric-infrastructure claims, and a $26B adversarial public-cost model; private creditor seniority remains separate from public hold-harmless proof.

Rev0353 adds X-37566 reserve-margin stress and River Bend project scale: initial 330 MW utility capacity for 245 MW critical IT load, possible 1,000 MW utility-capacity phase, and major private financing. These show possible exposure scale; they do not by themselves prove public loss allocation. Rev0355 adds River Bend public-instrument discipline: Entergy utility-capacity/timeline evidence (330 MW utility capacity for 245 MW critical IT load), local IDB/PILOT leaseback and up-to-$90M/year revenue claims, an IDB distribution-schedule claim, rebate-sequencing evidence, and an official parish public-records route. These sources make the public-upside claim auditable but keep certification blocked until the actual PILOT lease, distribution resolution, utility-service/tariff terms, switchyard/line-cost assignment, water transfer agreement, exemption/Quality Jobs awards, and load-vs-forecast/ratebase evidence are bound.
public_balance_sheet_register.expected_loss: Unknown; expected public cost depends on forecast accuracy, tariff design, minimum-bill/collateral terms, and whether load materializes
public_balance_sheet_register.stress_scenario: AI load growth or speculative compute overbuild accelerates grid/water investments; load later delays, relocates, self-supplies, underperforms, or receives special tariff treatment, leaving network upgrades, reliability costs, water capacity, or foregone tax revenue on ordinary claimants.
public_balance_sheet_register.funding_source: utility rates, municipal water/sewer charges, public bonds, tax abatements, federal/state energy incentives, interconnection fees, and public loan/guarantee programs
public_balance_sheet_register.loss_sharing: Require direct assignment of upgrades, upfront deposits, collateral, minimum bills, demand ratchets, termination charges, exit fees, capacity-reassignment constraints, interruptibility/flexibility commitments, water-impact fees, reporting, transparency, and no-stranded-cost clauses before socialized ratebase recovery. For Pennsylvania/PPL specifically, test 50 MW/75 MW LP-6 thresholds, minimum 10-year ESAs, enhanced security, exit fees, upgrade/CIAC treatment, non-critical load segmentation, and $11 million USR assignment against the final tariff and signed agreements. For Louisiana, test Entergy full-cost-service and customer-benefit claims against Kunkel testimony, the U-37425 docket record, final ESA term, FAC credit treatment, sponsor/lease guarantees, and any Blue Owl/Beignet abandonment or substitution rights. Louisiana loss-sharing now turns on monitorable order conditions, not slogans: CIAC zeroing, parent guaranty/collateral, minimum monthly charge true-up, early-termination fee use, annual confidential reports, and no other-customer recovery for customer-caused upgrades. Rev0352 loss-sharing audit now follows the LPSC guideline checklist: full network/interconnection cost assignment, no material uncompensated transmission shift, full incremental revenue-requirement recovery, no cross-subsidization, early-termination protection, enforceable curtailment, fuel-risk assignment, environmental mitigation, and ongoing reporting. Rev0353 distinguishes private loss-sharing from public loss-sharing. Google-backed lease/pass-through obligations and senior secured note liens protect project finance, while public/ratepayer loss-sharing still depends on utility tariff, ESA, water, incentive, and stranded-cost instruments. Rev0354: River Bend adds specific private-creditor and incentive/water claims, but private creditor seniority, PILOT/rebate, sales/use tax exemption, and switchyard/line cost assignment must be proven with primary instruments before being treated as public hold-harmless.
public_balance_sheet_register.public_upside_recovery: Tariff premiums, clawbacks, public data reporting, community-benefit payments, tax-abatement recapture, water mitigation fees, load-flexibility commitments, low-income program contributions, energy-efficiency contributions, and enforceable service or investment milestones. For Virginia, score the $928 million FY23 sales/use tax exemption and 90 percent industry uptake against clawbacks, local revenue dependence, water mitigation, and service-wealth protections. Rev0350 requires project benefits to be enforceable, not promotional: $2.65B claimed customer benefits need signed agreement, order, measurement, clawback, and reporting hooks. Rev0351 requires U-37425 benefit claims and U-37882 Fair Share Plus claims to be verified against signed agreements, Commission orders, low-income/weatherization contribution terms, and post-approval reporting. Rev0352 treats customer-savings, Power to Care, weatherization, and sustainability claims as provisional until they can be matched to enforceable ESA/order conditions and monitored actuals. Rev0353 adds expected data-center tax-rebate/Quality Jobs incentives and water infrastructure claims, creating a concrete clawback/public-upside question rather than a generic subsidy question.
public_balance_sheet_register.ordinary_claimant_protection: No cost shift to existing residential/small-business ratepayers; protect low-income utility customers, water users, rural/tribal claimants, and local public-service budgets Ordinary ratepayers, parish taxpayers, school/sheriff taxing bodies, and water users remain senior unless the signed utility-service, incentive, water, and rebate instruments prove no cost shift.
public_balance_sheet_register.sunset_or_review: Quarterly while the FERC large-load docket and major co-location/tariff proceedings remain live; annual load-forecast, ratebase, water, and subsidy audit thereafter.

seniority_waterfall.stress_status: Should not be senior unless cost assignment, reliability obligations, and water duties are explicit.
seniority_waterfall.notes: Speed-to-power can dominate slower household affordability and water-claim review; Ohio/Virginia tariff terms show uptime requests must be subordinated to minimum-term, collateral, and cost-assignment duties. PPL LP-6 shows speed-to-power must be subordinated to ESA terms, security, exit fees, non-critical load segmentation, and cost assignment. Louisiana U-37425 shows uptime and speed-to-power cannot outrank final ESA/CIAC transparency and commission review. Rev0351: U-37425 written-order protections and U-37882 procedural controls must keep existing households ahead of hyperscale uptime claims until conditions are auditable. Rev0352: households and small businesses remain senior unless the guideline matrix proves no cross-subsidy, early-termination exposure, fuel/FAC shift, or environmental/local-cost migration. Rev0353: households/small businesses remain senior only if resource-adequacy, network, fuel, water, and incentive costs are contractually insulated; private Google/Hut 8 financing evidence does not automatically prove that insulation.
